scope.flow: MevCapture extension fee applied to exactIn vs exactOut swaps in a pool
scope.environment: AMM pool with MevCapture extension recording beginning-of-block tick and charging fee proportional to tick distance

statements.text: At the beginning of the block, the pool is at tick X.
MevCapture records the pool tick at the beginning of the block and charges additional fee proportional to the distance between the post-swap tick and that beginning-of-block tick.
For exactIn swaps, the MevCapture additional fee is taken on the output amount, so amountOut = amountOut - additionalFee.
For exactOut swaps, the MevCapture additional fee is added to the input amount, so amountIn += additionalFee.
Because the exactOut output amount is smaller than the exactIn amountOut, the required amountIn and resulting price impact are smaller, moving the price by G ticks with G < Z.
For the same received output amount, the MevCapture additional fee charged should be equal across the exactIn and exactOut swap paths, so neither path overpays or underpays relative to the other.
The MevCapture additional fee should be proportional to the actual tick distance moved by the swap (|post-swap tick - beginning-of-block tick| * fee) consistently for both swap paths.
most of the time one of the paths (ExactIn swap, ExactOut swap) overpays/underpays in comparison to the other

ambiguities: Report does not state who calls the swap or any authorization condition; user is generic.
No concrete numeric values for X, Z, G, fee, amountIn or amountOut are given, so the quantitative overpay/underpay is not fixed.
The report describes a hypothetical scenario ('lets imagine', 'what if') rather than an observed transaction; no actual trigger is supplied.
Whether exactOut is superior depends on the specific tick distance and fee values; the report asserts it for the outlined scenario only.
